summary: This is a Product class that represents a single product with a name and price. It provides getter and setter methods to access and modify these properties, while keeping the actual properties private so they can only be changed through these controlled methods. The constructor accepts an optional name parameter to set up the product when it's created.

explanations.5: The `private` keyword means this property can only be accessed from inside this class, not from outside; the type hint `string` means it must always hold text.
explanations.6: Similar to line 5, but this property holds a decimal number (like 19.99) instead of text.
explanations.8: The constructor is a special method that runs automatically when you create a new Product; the `string $name=''` means it accepts a name parameter but defaults to an empty string if you don't provide one.
explanations.10: The constructor only calls the setter for name, but notice it doesn't set the price at all—that seems like it might be a bug since the constructor accepts a price parameter that's never used.
